rows.name: sort-integer-1000
rows.source: set v {};for {set i 1000} {$i>0} {incr i -1} {lappend v $i};lindex [lsort -integer $v] end

rows.name: sort-stride-200
rows.source: set v {};for {set i 200} {$i>0} {incr i -1} {lappend v rack$i $i};lindex [lsort -stride 2 -index 1 -integer $v] end

rows.name: sort-indices-500
rows.source: set v {};for {set i 500} {$i>0} {incr i -1} {lappend v $i};lindex [lsort -integer -indices $v] end

rows.name: sort-nested-100
rows.source: set v {};for {set i 100} {$i>0} {incr i -1} {lappend v [list rack$i [list value $i]]};lindex [lsort -integer -index {1 1} $v] 0

rows.name: sort-command-100
rows.source: proc cmp {a b} {expr {$a-$b}};set v {};for {set i 100} {$i>0} {incr i -1} {lappend v $i};lindex [lsort -command cmp $v] end

rows.name: sort-unique-200
rows.source: set v {};for {set i 200} {$i>0} {incr i -1} {lappend v row$i [expr {$i%10}]};llength [lsort -stride 2 -index 1 -integer -unique $v]

scope: Six small warm-session sorting workloads, native and Node measured separately on one host; exact results verified. Different host adapters; no full application, peak memory or cross-platform acceptance.
